question: The Government Budget is a statement of estimates of the government receipts and government expenditure for the coming financial year. The financial year for India is the period from _____to______
solution:
The correct answer is __**April 1 to March 31.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **financial year **for India is the period from **April 1 to March 31.**
 
• This means that the **government budget **estimates for the financial year are prepared based on the **expected receipts and expenditure** during this period.
 
• The government receipts include revenue from **taxes, non-tax sources, and borrowings**, while the government expenditure includes both **revenue and capital expenditure** on various sectors such as **defense, education, healthcare, infrastructure**, etc.
 
• The budget is an important tool for **fiscal management and policy-making**, as it reflects the government's priorities and goals for the economy and society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The financial year for India was earlier from **May 1 to April 30,** but it was changed to April 1 to March 31 in 1867.
 
• The government presents the budget in the Parliament in the form of two documents: the** Union Budget**, which includes the estimates for the central government, and the** State Budgets**, which include the estimates for the state governments.
 
• The budget also includes various measures to promote **economic growth, reduce fiscal deficits, and address social and welfare issues.**
 
• The government uses various fiscal instruments such as** taxes, subsidies, and transfers** to achieve its budgetary objectives.
 
• The budget is subject to approval by the **Parliament** and may be revised during the year if there are significant changes in the economic and financial situation.
